meta.note: machine-written (Claude), not reviewed by a native speaker
meta.about: Words the Friuli content uses that Wiktionary lacks (companion/bin/lexicon-build --coverage --lang it lists them): the folklore of Nonno Bepi's stories (sbilfs, krivapete, the Orcolat), Friulian words (fogolâr, pignarûl, cramaro), the region's places as the content names them (the Collio, Cormòns, Carnia, Monte Lussari, Duino, Nova Gorica), the night sky's meteor showers, an imperative with its pronoun joined (arrotolala), the elided c'è, dov'è, cos'è (Wiktionary has them in English only, or as a junk infinitive), and, marked override, a better meaning for suo, whose German through English was sein; n. Each has its meaning in German and Slovene (meanings), so a learner from either reads it in their own language, flagged machine-written. Left out: the people's names (the villagers' come from the cast), the interjections and sounds but eh, the most frequent (hm, shh, bzz), and the wrong choices the dialogs offer on purpose (venirò, vedito). Since 2026-11-01 also the words the course's printed sheets left off for want of a meaning (the everyday verbs, adverbs, nouns and expressions of A1, A2 and B1: guardare, mai, il treno, c'era una volta), written for a child (German first, Slovene, English), each with the forms the Italian content uses (the course, the grammar book, the Friuli culture, the packs) and their grammar; a reflexive verb's forms with their pronoun (si lava, mi sono lavata), so the plain verb's (gira il frico) aren't taken for it; the forms written by hand and checked against Wiktionary's (kaikki.org, English and German Wiktionary), the meanings written, not copied (docs/plans/05-built/it-print-meanings.md).
